text:
sam: quick thread — I'm proposing we unify the client-facing surface into a single thin SDK + optional edge shim. goal: simpler routing policies, consistent telemetry and a smoother canary rollout UX.

priya: curious — thin SDK + shim how is that materially different from the gateway-adapter we've debated?

sam: main diff: shim is strictly translation + header propagation, no auth/quotas logic. keeps quota enforcement in control plane/gateway but lets SDK optimize batching/prefetching. tiny binary on customer edge or sidecar.

lee: that avoids centralized gateway becoming a choke point. but where do we surface per-route quotas in console? ops wants per-customer per-route controls.

marcus: console proposal: show two quota layers — control-plane quotas (hard enforcement) and client-suggested soft budgets (SDK hints). UI: per-model + per-route tabs, rollout slider for canary %, and a telemetry pane with token-latency hist + QPS by route.

priya: can we still support REST-first customers who don't want SDKs? SDK adoption isn't 100%.

sam: yes — shim exposes REST/gRPC endpoints. SDK talks to shim locally; shim translates to internal protobuf over mTLS. So REST clients keep same integration.

lee: we need to be explicit about header propagation: tenant id, request-id, route-id, and sampling flags. suggestion: require `x-rd-tenant`, `x-rd-route`, `x-rd-trace` from shim to gateway.

marcus: agreed. telemetry needs consistent tag set. we should standardize metric labels: service, route, model, variant, tenant, canary_bucket. console will rely on those.

priya: ops concern: how do we handle quotas enforcement race when both SDK and gateway send hints? e.g., SDK decides to batch 10 requests => bursts.

sam: enforce quota at gateway. SDK/shim can request pre-alloc tokens via a cheap token-check API: `POST /quota/check {tenant, route, tokens}` returning `{ granted: n }`. If denied, SDK backoff.

lee: that token-check needs to be tiny and local — hitting control plane on every request defeats latency SLO. make it a local cache with TTL and token bucket refill policy.

marcus: rollout UX: console should let product teams set canary policies: percent-of-tenants, percent-of-traffic, header-based targeting (org IDs), and automatic rollback triggers (error rate, latency regressions, embedding-quality drift).

priya: automatic rollback triggers need telemetry thresholds and baselines. we'll need a small eval harness to run golden prompts and measure cosine-sim/embedding drift for model swaps.

sam: yes — Redwood Optimize integration: tie quality monitors to rollout gates. console shows pass/fail metrics.

lee: one more: protobuf vs json payloads. if shim translates REST->proto, we must document canonical proto and keep compatibility rules (field deprecations only). Also provide a human-readable JSON wire format for debugging.

marcus: propose we version the proto and expose `Accept-Version` headers. rollout plan: start with opt-in beta tenants, then a 10% traffic canary for 48h, then 50% for 24h, then GA. console will automate steps and require two manual approvals before 50% and GA.

priya: sounds reasonable. what's the telemetry story during canary? we need sampling keys so we can compare baseline vs canary.

sam: shim will tag `canary_bucket` and `canary_id` in every request; gateway metrics aggregator will create split dashboards. also emit raw traces with `route` + `model_variant` attributes for flamegraphs.

lee: any perf numbers? what's the added latency from shim translation?

sam: microbenchmarks: shim translation <1ms median, <3ms p95 in our PoC when co-located as sidecar. token-check local cache reduces control-plane calls by ~95%. network hop to gateway still dominates.

marcus: security: shim must enforce mTLS to gateway. keys rotated via KMS. console will show key expiry and rotation events.

priya: billing/quotas UI: show projected monthly cost under current batching/quantization settings. tie to usage alerts.

lee: telemetry retention? product wants 90d retention for token lat/loss metrics but infra wants 7d for raw traces. propose aggregated metrics 90d, full traces 14d by default.

sam: fine. add premium retention as add-on.

marcus: ops-bot:rollout-checklist created -> checklist: 1) proto spec committed, 2) shim binary + tests, 3) console rollout UI, 4) canary automation script, 5) telemetry dashboards, 6) quota token-check API deployed.

priya: +1 to checklist. i'll own the console pieces.

lee: i'll own shim and header propagation. sam will own protocol+gateway changes. marcus owns rollout automation and dashboards.

sam: great. let's aim for an internal beta in 3 weeks. if anyone sees a blocker call it out now.

priya: minor blocker: docs + SDK packaging for node/python. will start drafts tomorrow.

lee: dev note: proto snippet for comment: ```proto
syntax = "proto3";
message InferenceRequest {
  string tenant = 1;
  string route = 2;
  bytes input = 3;
  map<string,string> metadata = 4;
}
```

sam: thanks. if no objections i'll open RFC and a dev-issue to track the checklist. :thumbsup: 

marcus: :thumbsup:  , also please add a telemetry example query for baseline vs canary: `rate(token_latency_bucket[5m]) by (canary_bucket)`

console-bot: Created RFC: https://rdrw.internal/rfc/1234 — assigned owners sam/lee/priya/marcus.

ops-bot: Deployed quota-token-check service to staging cluster `quota-stg`.
